The navigation map updates async on a thread in Godot 4.4 by default.
If you do not want that you can disable it in the project settings under `navigation/world/map_use_async_iterations`.

In general a navigation map query does not work in a ready function at game start. The map graph is empty as no sync has happened at that point and all kinds of other nodes might not even have fully loaded or send their navmesh data. The only thing that was holding that old script together was map_force_update() code smell and duct-tape.

I suggest that you update your code and instead use either the `map_changed` signal or check the `iteration_id` of the map. Those two can reliably tell you when a map has synced and build a new pathfinding graph. Everything else is just luck and guesswork.

Thank you for the quick reply @smix8! But even if I move the `map_get_path` call into `_physics_process` it always returns an empty Array. It never settles.

Or do you mean that something needs to be re-baked as a response to that signal?

EDIT: And disabling the async iterations did not help

> Or do you mean that something needs to be re-baked as a response to that signal?

No, you dont need to do anything except maybe wait (longer).

The main issue in that example script is that you forgot to set the navigation map active. So outside of your single map_force_update() call this map never updates on its own.

Add `NavigationServer2D.map_set_active(_nav_map_rid, true)` to your script to set the map active so that it auto-syncs on all changes.

If I query a path in process() I get a navigation path immediately with your script after the map is set active. With physics process it takes a tick extra. Likely because by the time process() runs (which is later in the main loop) the threaded map update has already finished. The physics_process() does run early and also not every frame so that is unreliable.

If you poll `map_get_iteration_id()` at the start that value is usually 0 because the map has not synced. Each time the map has finished building a new map iteration, aka has finished the threaded update, that iteration id gets increased by +1. So if that function returns >1 you know it has at least synced one time since game start. The map_changed signal gets emitted afterward. That signal has a RID parameter with the map that got changed so you need to check if it is the map RID that you are interested in.

> Add NavigationServer2D.map_set_active(_nav_map_rid, true) to your script to set the map active so that it auto-syncs on all changes.

That did the trick! Thank you so much! I was tearing my hair out.

Don't know if I should close this issue or not? The behavior has definitely changed, but it's more one of those reverse bugs that I was talking about.
Closing as it's not really a regression. More of a quirk that used to work. Don't want to add it to a list of probably more interesting/important issues.
